title: Multimarginal flow matching with optimal transport potentials
claim: Prior flow methods ignore or rigidly interpolate intermediate marginals; ours uses soft tunable potentials to produce smooth, flexible trajectories.
layout: Left 2x3 grid of trajectory panels; right large decomposition panel with math
description: The left side is a grid of small panels. All share a time axis from 0 to 1, with red start points, green end points, and orange and brown intermediate marginal points. The top row shows the baselines. CFM draws straight lines that ignore the intermediate points. Multimarginal CFM draws piecewise-linear lines with sharp kinks. MMFM/3MSBM draws fixed smooth interpolations. The bottom row is labelled OTP-FM (ours). Its three panels vary strength w, width τ and λ shape, using purple curves of different shades, with λ(t) bump profiles drawn along the bottom. The right side is a large panel headed by the equation X_t = X_base + α Σ X_corr. It overlays dashed CFM paths and solid OTP-FM paths for different α values. Orange and brown arrows mark the corrections at t1 and t2, and below them are Gaussian bumps for λ(t).
caption: (Left) Comparing standard CFM — straight-line trajectories ignoring intermediate marginals; multimarginal CFM — stitching CFM trajectories piecewise between consecutive marginals; prescriptive approaches such as MMFM and 3MSBM — using fixed interpolation strategies to smooth kinks; and OTP-FM, whose soft potential-driven dynamics with tunable strength w, temporal width τ, and λ shape yields smooth and flexible trajectories. (Right) Method overview: trajectories Xt are decomposed as a base CFM path Xbase k,t that are gradually scaled by the curriculum parameter α to converge to the OTP-FM solution.
abstract: Flow matching (FM) has emerged as a powerful framework for learning dynamic transport maps between two empirical distributions. However, less explored is the setting with intermediate observed marginals that can help constrain the flows between the endpoints. This "multimarginal" regime is central to modeling temporal evolution in dynamical systems in many scientific domains that can sample sequential distributions. We tackle this problem with a novel approach that leverages the connection between FM and dynamic optimal transport (OT), softly steering the flow towards the intermediate marginals through potential terms in the dynamic OT action. By extending the conditional FM learning target to incorporate these potentials, we derive an efficient, simulation-free algorithm for multimarginal FM that offers considerable flexibility in the spatiotemporal dynamics of the learned flows. We demonstrate state-of-the-art performance and training efficiency of OT-potential FM (OTP-FM) on diverse single-cell RNA sequencing, oceanographic, and meteorological datasets. Our code is available at https://github.com/Bexorg-Inc/OTP-FM.
